title: Standard
description: A standard issued by a unit (cyber security, a platform owner, a practice). It is a list of requirements that applications, code and infrastructure must meet.

id.description: Unique kebab-case id of the standard, e.g. "secure-logging".

summary.description: One or two sentences: what the standard protects or achieves.

owner.description: Id of the team (from the teams list) that issues and maintains this standard.

category.description: Id of the category (from the categories list) this is grouped under in the libraries and in search, e.g. "cloud".

practice.description: Id of the practice (from the practices list) this belongs to, e.g. "security". The owners of that practice may change it. Leave out when it belongs to no practice.

platform.description: Id of the platform (from the platforms list) this belongs to, e.g. "google-cloud". The owners of that platform may change it. Leave out when it belongs to no platform.

scope.description: What it covers and what it does not, in plain words, e.g. "All services that handle customer data. Batch jobs are out of scope."

tiers.description: Ids of the application tiers this standard applies to. Leave out when it applies to ALL tiers.

languages.description: Ids of the programming languages this standard is specific to. Leave out when it does not depend on the language.

environments.description: Ids of the environments this standard applies to, e.g. ["production"]. Leave out when it applies to ALL environments.

status.description: Life-cycle state. "draft" = being written, hidden from consumers. "active" = in use (default when left out). "deprecated" = retired, kept for reference.

replacedBy.description: For a deprecated standard: id of the standard to use instead.

review.description: Periodic review by the owner team.

intervalMonths.description: How often the owner must confirm the process is still correct.

lastReviewedAt.description: Date of the last review, YYYY-MM-DD. Leave out if never reviewed.

exceptionProcessId.description: Id of the process to follow to ask for an exception to this standard.

kind.description: "skill" = instructions an AI coding assistant can run to do the work in self-service, e.g. a skill that updates the IaC repository.

description.description: What it does for the reader.

id.description: Stable id people and tools cite, upper case with dashes, e.g. "SEC-LOG-01". Never reused for another rule.

title.description: Short name of the rule, e.g. "No secrets in logs".

level.description: "must" = mandatory, an exception is needed to deviate. "should" = expected, deviate only with a good reason. "may" = optional good practice.

statement.description: The rule itself, one testable sentence or two.

rationale.description: Why the rule exists: the risk it removes.

guidance.description: How to comply, one concrete action per item.

method.description: "automated" = a pipeline or scanner checks it. "review" = checked when code is reviewed. "manual" = checked by a person outside code review, e.g. an audit.

description.description: What checks it, e.g. "Secret scanner in the build pipeline".

review.description: What a reviewer (person or agent) looks for in a pull request.

lookFor.description: Concrete signs of a violation, one per item.

paths.description: File patterns where this matters, e.g. "**/*.go", "terraform/**". Leave out for all files.

severity.description: How a finding is reported. Default: blocker for must, warning for should, info for may.

tiers.description: Narrow this requirement to some tiers. Leave out to follow the standard.

languages.description: Narrow this requirement to some languages. Leave out to follow the standard.

environments.description: Narrow this requirement to some environments. Leave out to follow the standard.

processId.description: Id of a process that helps to meet this requirement.
